# Northline

The sales and operations system for Northline Exhaust Co., an invented maker
of heavy-duty truck exhaust parts. A demo app on synthetic data: every record
in it is made up, and nothing here describes a real company, person or
customer.

SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5, TypeScript, Postgres with no ORM. Every request runs in
a transaction as the signed-in person, and row-level security in Postgres
decides what they may read and change.

## Getting in

The site may sit behind one shared password (a form at /gate sets a signed
cookie). Endpoints that carry their own secret skip it: /api/mcp, the cron
runs and the mail webhook.

An agent with an MCP token should use /api/mcp rather than the pages: it
speaks MCP over HTTP, its read tools answer directly, and anything that
changes data becomes a proposal for a person in /workspace. /settings/mcp
mints a token.

## Signing in

Inside the site there are no passwords. GET /signin lists the people you can be and a POST
with `userId` sets a signed cookie. Every other path redirects to /signin
without one. Reads and writes are scoped to whoever the cookie names.

## Routes

Filters and sorts are query parameters, so every view is a link that can be
handed to someone else.

- /commitments               the board, six lanes. ?who=mine|all
- /commitments/<id>          one commitment: scope, delivery, quotes, notes
- /commitments/answer        the question asked when a window closes short
- /accounts                  the account book. ?q ?state ?group ?quiet ?open ?sort ?page ?who
- /accounts/<customer_no>    one account: people, revenue, orders, activity
- /parts                     the part list. ?q ?family ?short ?reorder ?sort
- /parts/<item_no>           one part: stock, price, cost, sales, buyers, siblings
- /vendors                   the vendor list. ?q ?all
- /vendors/<vendor_no>       one vendor: terms, contacts, parts supplied
- /search                    accounts, parts and vendors in one page. ?q
- /operations                the daily ERP export: upload, review, apply. ?snapshot
- /operations/forecast       when each open line will really ship. ?status ?vendor ?wc ?customer ?who
- /warehouse                 bins, the stock ledger, picks, counts. ?part
- /automations               the rule list
- /automations/new           build a rule
- /automations/<id>          one rule and what it has done
- /rfq                       turn a customer email into a draft quote
- /rfq/<id>                  one draft: what was read, what was checked
- /ask                       ask a question in plain English
- /ask/<id>                  one conversation and any proposal waiting

## Reading the pages

Record names are anchors to the record's own URL, so the graph can be walked
by following links. Every page has one `<main id="content">` and one `<h1>`,
and its browser title names the record. Section headings carry ids that work
as anchors, for example /commitments/3014#answers.

There is no public JSON API. SvelteKit serves each page's load data at
`<route>/__data.json`, which is an internal shape and is not a contract.

## Tools for an agent

An assistant lives at /ask with fourteen tools. Seven read (search accounts,
read an account, read a commitment, list windows closed short, read a part,
run a read-only SQL query, test an automation rule). Two write directly and
are additive only (add a note, add a next step). Four write and are gated:
they cannot run from a model at all, only be proposed for a person to
approve. Read tools answer as JSON text; there is no output schema yet.

An MCP server over HTTP is being built on another branch. Until it is
merged, an outside agent reads this app through its pages.

## What an agent must not do

Nothing that changes a business record can be done by an agent without a
person approving it. That is enforced in the SQL functions, not in a prompt:
every write claims a request id, requires an active user, checks the field
rules, locks on the row's version and writes an audit row. A refused write
raises an NL4xx code.
